cards.text: Aaron is Israel's priest, and his sons serve as priests with him. Now Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu take their censers, put fire in them and add incense. Then they offer it before the LORD.

cards.question: The fire Nadab and Abihu offered before the LORD was what the LORD had commanded.
Right after Nadab and Abihu offer their fire, ___ comes out from the presence of the LORD.

cards.text: It consumes them, and they die right there in the presence of the LORD. Friend, that's a heavy moment.
Then Moses, Israel's leader, says to Aaron, “This is what the LORD meant when He said: ‘To those who come near Me I will show My holiness, and in the sight of all the people I will reveal My glory.’”

cards.question: Moses has just told Aaron what the LORD meant. How does Aaron respond?

answers.text: He cries out to the LORD

cards.text: Moses calls over Mishael and Elzaphan, sons of Aaron's uncle Uzziel. He tells them to carry their cousins' bodies away from the front of the sanctuary.

cards.question: Moses tells Mishael and Elzaphan to carry the bodies of their cousins ___ the camp.

cards.text: So they carry them out, still in their tunics, just as Moses directed. Then Moses turns to Aaron and his sons Eleazar and Ithamar with instructions.

cards.question: Moses tells Aaron, Eleazar and Ithamar to tear their garments and mourn.
Who does Moses say may mourn over the fire the LORD has ignited?

answers.text: Only the Levites in the camp

cards.text: And Moses' warning is serious. If Aaron and his sons mourn like that, they will die, and the LORD will be angry with the whole congregation.

cards.question: Aaron and his sons must not go outside the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, or they will die. Why? The LORD's ___ oil is on them.

cards.text: Aaron and his sons do as Moses instructed. Then the LORD speaks to Aaron directly, not through Moses this time.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell Aaron and his sons not to do when they enter the Tent of Meeting?

cards.text: And it's a permanent statute for the generations to come, not a just-for-today thing. The priests also have to distinguish between the holy and the common, between the clean and the unclean.

cards.question: Why does the LORD want the priests to know the holy from the common and the clean from the unclean?

answers.text: So they can teach the Israelites His statutes
So they can settle disputes between the tribes
So they can decide who may enter the camp

cards.text: Then Moses tells Aaron and his remaining sons, Eleazar and Ithamar, about their share of the offerings: the grain offering eaten without leaven beside the altar, and the breast and thigh their families may eat in a clean place. Those breast and thigh portions belong to them and their children permanently, as the LORD has commanded.
Later, Moses searches carefully for the goat of the sin offering, like me hunting for a timer I SWEAR I just set down. And behold, it's been burned up.

cards.question: When Moses finds the goat burned up, he is ___ with Eleazar and Ithamar.
Moses asks why they didn't eat the sin offering in the holy place. What does he say it was given to them to do?

answers.text: Thank the LORD for the harvest
Mark the end of the eighth day

cards.text: Moses isn't done. He explains why they should have eaten it in the sanctuary area, as he commanded.

cards.question: Moses says the sin offering's blood was brought inside the holy place.

cards.text: Then Aaron, the one who stayed silent earlier, speaks up. He reminds Moses that this very day they presented their sin offering and burnt offering before the LORD, and then there's everything that has happened to him.

cards.question: So what does Aaron ask Moses about eating the sin offering that day?

answers.text: Would it have been acceptable to the LORD
Was it his job or his sons' job
Should it have been burned inside the camp

cards.question: When Moses hears Aaron's explanation, he is ___.

findings.problem: The card states facts from outside the passage: Aaron is Israel's priest and his sons serve as priests with him. Leviticus 10:1 doesn't say this, and no reference is given for it (for example Exodus 28:1 or Leviticus 8). The card cites only Leviticus 10:1.

rule.text: Every fact and every verse number comes from that text. Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "So they can decide who may enter the camp" is arguably right. Telling clean from unclean is how it was decided who had to stay outside the camp (Leviticus 13:46). A baker could argue for it. Replace it with an answer that has nothing to do with clean and unclean.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Outside the one timer joke (stop 2, card 2), the story cards read as plain summaries with almost no Papa Dorin voice. Examples are stop 1, cards 7, 9 and 14, and stop 2, cards 5 and 7. Holding back at the deaths in 10:1-7 fits the moment. The later scenes leave room for his storyteller lines, reactions and humor: Moses searching for the goat, Moses' anger, Aaron finally speaking up, and Moses being satisfied.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
